stories.headline: Demystifying AI finance: the supply chain, capital flows and global rivalry
stories.summary: On 9 November 2026, columnist Sajed ul Islam argued the AI boom is one of history's most capital-intensive industrial build-outs, with tech giants pledging hundreds of billions of dollars while the real story lies in physical supply chains. He argues Nvidia designs the chips, TSMC in Taiwan manufactures them, and SK Hynix and Samsung supply high-bandwidth memory, making Taiwan a chokepoint: if its fabs paused, he argues, the global AI revolution would halt.
stories.why_it_matters: AI, semiconductors and the US-China technology rivalry are now core BCS science-and-technology and economy topics, and the supply-chain map in this column — designers, foundries and memory makers — is the background every later chip-shortage or export-control story will assume.
stories.exam_facts: Columnist Sajed ul Islam, a senior banking executive and financial-markets specialist, argues investors face the acute fear of missing out on the AI shift, backed by surging earnings and massive forecasted growth; he argues chip designers such as Nvidia and AMD draw blueprints but manufacture nothing; TSMC, Intel Foundry and GlobalFoundries fabricate chips using extreme ultraviolet light; memory specialists SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron Technology supply high-bandwidth memory; he argues building an advanced AI system resembles constructing a fleet of spacecraft, with no single company acting alone.
stories.exam_relevance: AI, semiconductors, capital flows, geopolitics — BCS science & technology and economy topics.
stories.key_people: Sajed ul Islam, columnist, senior banking executive
stories.figures: Column published 9 November 2026; tech giants pledge hundreds of billions of dollars; Nvidia the undisputed brain of the AI boom; TSMC the critical chokepoint in Taiwan.

stories.headline: Hasina seeks new passport to return in December; government swiftly rejects the request
stories.summary: Ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina asked Bangladesh on 9 November for a new passport and national identity card so she can return from two years of exile in India in December and surrender to a court. The government swiftly rejected the request, with State Minister Humaiun Kobir calling her a fugitive criminal and demanding extradition under the active Bangladesh-India treaty. She was sentenced to death in absentia last November over the 2024 crackdown in which the UN says as many as 1,400 people were killed.
stories.why_it_matters: The passport request, the death sentence and the extradition treaty together decide whether Hasina ever faces a Bangladeshi court, so this is the single story that frames every later report on her return, Dhaka-Delhi relations and the tribunal's verdicts.
stories.exam_facts: London-based Matrix Chambers wrote to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, saying Hasina's passport and NID had been revoked by the interim government and asking for new documents expeditiously on the basis of her Bangladeshi nationality; Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the foreign and law ministries were examining whether she was legally entitled to apply; her aides said the return date would be announced once formalities were complete; Hasina served as prime minister from 1996 to 2001 and again from 2009 to 2024, a total of 20 years; her Awami League, once the country's largest party, was banned after her fall and many colleagues are jailed or in exile; at a BNP parliamentary party meeting on 9 November, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the home minister said the government would act under the extradition treaty if she sought to return.
stories.exam_relevance: Extradition treaty, war-crimes tribunal, exile and return — recurring BCS/Bank current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Sheikh Hasina; Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs; Salahuddin Ahmed, Home Minister; Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner in Delhi; Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister
stories.figures: In India for 2 years; return promised in December; death sentence last November; as many as 1,400 killed in 2024 (UN); prime minister 1996-2001 and 2009-2024.

stories.headline: Russia and Bangladesh sign protocol to boost trade and economic cooperation
stories.summary: Russia and Bangladesh signed the protocol of the 5th meeting of their Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation, setting the guideline for further bilateral engagement and joint projects. Co-chairpersons of both sides signed after a two-day plenary session of government officials and business representatives. Talks covered trade and industrial cooperation, agriculture and energy, with both sides seeking stronger bilateral trade and economic ties.
stories.why_it_matters: The Intergovernmental Commission is the standing bilateral mechanism for trade, energy and scientific cooperation with Russia, so its protocol is the frame for future questions on Bangladesh-Russia trade, energy ties and joint projects.
stories.exam_facts: The commission is the Intergovernmental Commission (IGC) on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation, and this was its 5th meeting; the signed document incorporates the issues discussed at the meeting and will serve as a guideline for practical cooperation and implementation of joint projects; the protocol was signed by the co-chairpersons of the Russian and Bangladeshi sides following the plenary session; the Russian side thanked its Bangladeshi counterparts for their cooperation during the two-day meeting and hoped the agreements reached would produce tangible benefits for both countries.
stories.exam_relevance: Bilateral trade, intergovernmental commissions, Bangladesh-Russia relations — BCS foreign-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Co-chairpersons of the Russian and Bangladeshi sides of the IGC
stories.figures: 5th meeting of the IGC; two-day meeting; protocol signed 10 November 2026.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank doubles overseas medical treatment remittance limit to $30,000
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank has doubled the foreign-currency remittance limit for medical treatment abroad without prior approval, from $15,000 to $30,000, in a circular issued on 9 November. Authorised dealer banks may now also remit funds for secondary and higher secondary education abroad without prior approval, if free education is not available. The circular also allows remittance for regular academic studies through correspondence courses and tightens rules for depositing foreign currency brought in by resident Bangladeshis.
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign-exchange and remittance rules are staple Bank-exam material, and the $30,000 medical limit with the education easements is exactly the kind of current circular BCS and Bank papers test alongside the foreign-currency deposit rules.
stories.exam_facts: The previous medical treatment limit was $15,000; authorised dealer (AD) banks previously needed prior central-bank approval for school-level education remittances; the new provision covers secondary and higher secondary-equivalent studies, subject to verification that free education is not available; the correspondence-course facility previously covered only correspondence and distance certification courses for professional examinations, and now covers regular academic studies; foreign currency brought into the country by resident Bangladeshis can be credited to Resident Foreign Currency Deposit (RFCD) accounts only under tightened conditions; the decisions aim to ease outward remittance procedures and facilitate legitimate current-account transactions.
stories.exam_relevance: Banking, foreign-exchange regulation, remittance rules — core Bank exam material.
stories.figures: Medical limit $15,000 to $30,000; circular 9 November 2026; RFCD rules tightened.

stories.headline: Government calls Hasina's return moves 'merely political posturing'
stories.summary: Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said on 9 November that Sheikh Hasina's recent activities were merely political posturing and that she has no intention of returning from India. He said she was not taking the legal steps she should take to return, despite her stated plan to come back in December. Hasina faces a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly 2024 crackdown, and has lived in India since fleeing in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.
stories.why_it_matters: The prosecutor's 'political posturing' line and the death sentence are the government's legal answer to Hasina's return plan, so this story is the counterpoint students need to pair with the passport request itself.
stories.exam_facts: The Daily Star quoted Islam speaking to journalists at his office; State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir had ruled out issuing any travel document or passport to Hasina, describing her as a fugitive terrorist and a dictator; Bangladesh has sought her extradition from India, where she took refuge after leaving office; India has acknowledged receiving the extradition requests but has yet to announce a decision, with its foreign ministry saying the requests are being examined as part of its established processes; Hasina's Awami League government was toppled by a student-led uprising in August 2024.
stories.exam_relevance: Extradition, war-crimes tribunal, political rhetoric — BCS current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Md Aminul Islam, Chief Prosecutor; Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs
stories.figures: In India since August 2024; death sentence in absentia; return promised in December.

stories.headline: Bangladesh validates Multisectoral Action Plan for eye health 2027-2029
stories.summary: Bangladesh has validated its Multisectoral Action Plan for Eye Health for 2027-2029 at a national workshop held on 8 November at Hotel InterContinental, Dhaka. The plan treats eye health as a shared development priority, not only a health issue, because vision impairment affects education, employment, productivity and social participation. It brings together ministries including education, labour, agriculture, industries, women and children affairs and social welfare under the health ministry's lead.
stories.why_it_matters: Health policy and multi-ministry planning appear in BCS general-knowledge and health questions, and the 2027-2029 eye-health plan shows how Bangladesh now frames a single disease area as an education, employment and welfare issue at once.
stories.exam_facts: The Multisectoral National Platform on Eye Health was initiated by The Fred Hollows Foundation, with support from UNDP Bangladesh and in coordination with Sightsavers and other members of the International NGO Forum for Eye Health; the platform is led by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital; Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain attended as chief guest; Md Mohsin, joint secretary, chairs the platform and Syed Mehbub Ul Kadir, director (in-charge) of the National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital, gave the keynote presentation; the plan reflects Bangladesh's commitment to the global eye-health agenda and the momentum of the Global Summit on Eye Health; discussions covered strategic priorities, institutional roles and implementation milestones for coordinated action over 2027-2029.
stories.exam_relevance: Health policy, multisectoral planning, development partners — BCS general-knowledge topics.
stories.key_people: Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain, Minister of Health and Family Welfare; Md Mohsin, Joint Secretary; Syed Mehbub Ul Kadir, National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital

stories.headline: PM leaves for COP31 summit in Turkiye; to deliver Bangladesh's statement on 12 November
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will leave on 10 November for Turkiye to attend the COP31 World Leaders' Summit in Antalya on 11-12 November, delivering Bangladesh's statement at a plenary session on 12 November. Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury said bilateral meetings were being arranged with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the Australian prime minister, the president of Uzbekistan and the British foreign secretary, covering trade, investment and climate cooperation.
stories.why_it_matters: COP summits and Bangladesh's climate diplomacy are recurring BCS current-affairs topics, and the Antalya visit — with its bilateral meetings and the compensation question — sets up the COP31 outcomes students will be tested on next.
stories.exam_facts: The official visit runs from 10 to 12 November, with the prime minister leading the Bangladesh delegation; his spouse Zubaida Rahman, the environment minister, the two state ministers for foreign affairs and the prime minister's special assistant on environment will accompany him; a meeting with the administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is also being explored; on compensation for climate losses, Chowdhury said Bangladesh presents estimates of its damage at international forums and distinguished compensation from broader assistance and cooperation; COP, the Conference of the Parties, is the annual United Nations climate summit; detailed talks on Turkish firm Celebi's interest in ground handling at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's third terminal were unlikely during the visit.
stories.exam_relevance: COP, climate diplomacy, bilateral meetings — core BCS foreign-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister; Recep Tayyip Erdogan, President of Turkiye; Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, Foreign Secretary; Zubaida Rahman
stories.figures: Visit 10-12 November 2026; summit 11-12 November in Antalya; statement on 12 November.

stories.headline: Economy returns to expansion in October as PMI rises to 51.8
stories.summary: Bangladesh's economy returned to expansion in October after two consecutive months of contraction, with the overall Purchasing Managers' Index rising 3.2 points to 51.8. Agriculture led the recovery, its PMI up 6 points to 61.2 in a 14th consecutive month of expansion, while manufacturing rose 6.1 points to 50.9 and construction 2.5 points to 51.0. But demand indicators stayed weak in several sectors and business costs continued to rise.
stories.why_it_matters: PMI is the standard monthly gauge of economic activity that BCS and Bank papers use, and the October rebound to 51.8 after two months of contraction is the headline number for any question on Bangladesh's 2026 growth.
stories.exam_facts: The October reading was released jointly by the Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MCCI), Dhaka, and Policy Exchange Bangladesh on 9 November; in manufacturing, new orders, new export orders and factory output remained in contraction and order backlogs showed sharp contraction, while stocks of inputs, finished goods and imports returned to expansion; input prices recorded strong expansion, signalling persistent cost pressures; in construction, employment recovered to expansion after remaining unchanged in September, though new business and construction activity stayed in contraction; in agriculture, new business, business activity and employment continued to expand, while the order backlogs index also returned to expansion, though input costs remained on the rise.
stories.exam_relevance: PMI, economic indicators, sectoral growth — core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.figures: Overall PMI 51.8, up 3.2 points; agriculture 61.2, up 6; manufacturing 50.9, up 6.1; construction 51.0, up 2.5; October 2026.

stories.headline: Nine industrial groups join the billion-dollar club
stories.summary: Nine industrial groups crossed the one-billion-dollar threshold in import and export trade in the 2025-26 financial year, up from eight a year earlier, despite energy shortages and flat exports. Together they imported goods worth $9.83 billion, exported about $3.05 billion and paid Tk199.44 billion in customs duties and taxes, taking their combined trade to $14.55 billion — nearly 11 per cent of Bangladesh's total import-export trade of $119.33 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: Industrial concentration and export earnings are core economy topics, and the nine-group list with its $14.55 billion combined trade is the concrete data behind questions on Bangladesh's biggest business groups and their trade.
stories.exam_facts: The nine groups are Meghna Group of Industries (MGI), PRAN-RFL, South Korea's Youngone Corporation, Abul Khair, Square, BSRM, TK Group, Khair Kashem and Ha-Meem; City Group fell out of the club after its trade declined 41 per cent in a year; Khair Kashem entered for the first time after acquiring several operational factories; MGI leads the club with about $3.2691 billion in trade, up 14 per cent, and imported goods worth $2.6717 billion; around 600,000 people work for the nine groups; the billion-dollar club counts import spending including duties plus export earnings, not total sales or profits; Youngone and Ha-Meem are entirely export-oriented, while MGI, Abul Khair, BSRM, TK and Khair Kashem mainly serve the domestic market.
stories.exam_relevance: Industrial groups, trade data, exports — core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Mostafa Kamal, Chairman, Meghna Group of Industries
stories.figures: 9 groups (was 8); imports $9.83bn; exports $3.05bn; duties Tk199.44bn (about $1.63bn); combined $14.55bn; goods-only $12.87bn; total trade $119.33bn; about 600,000 workers.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank orders minimum cash margins on 10 Ramadan imports
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank has directed banks to charge the minimum possible cash margin when opening letters of credit for 10 essential commodities ahead of Ramadan, with the directive in force until 15 March 2027. The 10 items are rice, wheat and flour, onions, lentils, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices and dates. Banks must also give priority to opening these letters of credit to keep domestic supplies steady, under the central bank's authority in Section 45 of the Bank Company Act.
stories.why_it_matters: Ramadan price management through import financing is a recurring Bank-exam theme, and the 10-item list with minimum LC margins under Section 45 is the exact circular detail such questions are built from.
stories.exam_facts: The directive was issued in a circular sent to the chief executives of all banks on Sunday 8 November; banks must set cash-margin rates at the minimum level based on the banker-customer relationship; the move follows a 5 September 2024 circular requiring 100 per cent cash margins for letters of credit on certain imports, and an 11 November 2025 instruction to keep margins at a minimum for selected consumer goods, which remained in force until 31 March this year; the latest directive takes immediate effect and remains in force until 15 March 2027. Note: the circular's item is 'wheat and flour' as one item (Prothom Alo prints the list verbatim), though bdnews24 and TBS shorten it to 'wheat'.
stories.exam_relevance: Import financing, LC margins, Ramadan price management — Bank exam topics.
stories.figures: 10 items; in force until 15 March 2027; 100 per cent margin required by the 5 September 2024 circular.

stories.headline: Dhaka University keeps admission tests on schedule; HSC supplementary students miss out
stories.summary: Dhaka University has rejected the University Grants Commission's call to reconsider admission schedules and will keep its 2026-27 admission process on schedule, with applications closing on 25 November and tests starting on 5 December. As a result, students passing this year's HSC supplementary examinations, which begin on 1 December, cannot sit the university's admission tests. The university says delaying by two to three months would create another session jam after Covid-19 disruptions.
stories.why_it_matters: Admission policy and the HSC supplementary examinations are the most immediate Jobs & Education topic for 2026 candidates, and the 1 December date with DU's 25 November deadline is the clash of dates exam papers will ask about.
stories.exam_facts: HSC and equivalent results were published on 31 October: of 1,240,798 candidates under 11 education boards, 646,685 passed and 422,905 failed in one or two subjects — 298,040 in one subject and 124,865 in two; supplementary examinations, for candidates failing in a maximum of two subjects, are being held for the first time this year; students whose results change after re-scrutiny, due on 23 November, may still apply; the UGC decided public universities would take first-year honours applications from January next year, with tests from February, but no Dhaka University representative attended the meeting; MBBS and BDS admission tests are scheduled for 18 December; UGC chairman Professor Mamun Ahmed asked universities to consider Ramadan when setting schedules.
stories.exam_relevance: University admission, HSC examinations, UGC policy — core Jobs & Education topics.
stories.key_people: Professor Mohammad Almujaddade Alfasane, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, University of Dhaka; Professor Mamun Ahmed, Chairman, University Grants Commission
stories.figures: Applications close 25 November; tests from 5 December; supplementary exams begin 1 December; 646,685 passed of 1,240,798; 422,905 failed in one or two subjects.

stories.headline: Workers' side seeks Tk32,000 minimum wage in RMG sector
stories.summary: The workers' side has proposed a minimum monthly wage of Tk32,000 for readymade garment workers, and Tk30,000 for new or apprentice workers, at the Minimum Wage Board's second meeting on 9 November. Workers' representative Babul Akhter said a worker needs Tk45,000 to Tk60,000 a month for a family of four to live decently. The board aims to finalise the new wage structure by December, with higher wages paid in the first week of January.
stories.why_it_matters: The RMG minimum wage is Bangladesh's biggest labour-economics question, and the workers' Tk32,000 demand against the Tk45,000-60,000 living-cost figure frames every later story on the wage board, factory unrest and export competitiveness.
stories.exam_facts: The proposal is for Grade 4 workers, with the Tk32,000 figure set against industry capacity and the overall situation; the meeting was held at the board's office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, and lasted three hours, chaired by Syed Azad Subhani; the employers' side failed to submit its written proposal, asked for seven working days and was granted four; the chairman said the board would move forward even if employers miss the next meeting; board members will visit garment factories of all categories this week, and independent member Professor Mosleh Uddin Ahmed will review international wage indicators, possibly consulting Dhaka University's Institute of Business Administration.
stories.exam_relevance: Minimum wage, RMG sector, labour economics — core BCS/Bank economy topics.

stories.headline: ICB in a bind as Tk3,000 crore Beximco Sukuk nears maturity
stories.summary: The Investment Corporation of Bangladesh, trustee of Beximco's Green Sukuk, faces a dilemma over the bond's outstanding Tk2,800 crore, due for repayment by 23 December as the five-year Islamic instrument matures. ICB cannot declare a default because Beximco still pays yields from its Teesta Solar plant's cash flows, yet recovery of the full amount by maturity is uncertain. The exposure spans 22 banks, raising fears of more classified investments if repayment fails.
stories.why_it_matters: Sukuk, classified investments and trustee duties are core Bank-exam finance topics, and the Tk2,800 crore Beximco repayment deadline of 23 December is the live case that ties Islamic finance to banking-sector stability.
stories.exam_facts: Beximco, owned by Salman F Rahman, former private industry and investment adviser to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, raised Tk3,000 crore in 2021 through the country's first private-sector Shariah-compliant Green Sukuk, of which about Tk200 crore was converted into shares; the remaining Tk2,800 crore is due to sukuk holders by 23 December; foreign investors Revival Global and Adsum Capital have expressed interest, while Beximco opposes Adsum's proposed acquisition of the Teesta Solar project; the sukuk's periodic yield payments continue from solar-plant cash flows; the repayment crisis threatens investor confidence and wider banking stability.
stories.exam_relevance: Sukuk, Islamic finance, classified investments, banking stability — core Bank exam topics.
stories.figures: Tk3,000 crore raised in 2021; Tk2,800 crore outstanding; Tk200 crore converted to shares; due 23 December; 22 banks exposed.

stories.headline: Yarn import row: PM asks committee to propose solution by 20 November
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed a committee led by the commerce minister to propose a solution to the yarn-import row by 20 November, after garment exporters and local textile mill owners presented opposing arguments at a meeting on 9 November. Exporters, especially knitwear makers, rely on duty-free yarn imports under bond facilities, while mill owners say cheaper imports undercut local yarn. Since early September, imports under bond require a bank guarantee equal to the yarn's value.
stories.why_it_matters: The yarn dispute pits exporters against domestic mills over bond facilities, and the 20 November committee deadline is the date that decides whether knitwear exporters keep duty-free yarn or local spinners gain protection.
stories.exam_facts: The meeting was held at the Secretariat on 9 November between exporters, mill owners and the prime minister; BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan Babu said the prime minister directed the committee to prepare and submit its report by 20 November, with a decision to follow; mill owners allege some exporters import yarn under bond facilities but sell it in the domestic market instead of using it for export garments; under the new system the bank guarantee is released only after exporters prove the yarn was used for export garments and export proceeds were repatriated; yarn is a major raw material for garments, particularly knitwear exporters.
stories.exam_relevance: RMG inputs, bond facilities, trade policy — BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Mahmud Hasan Khan Babu, President, BGMEA
stories.figures: Committee report due 20 November; bank guarantee equal to imported yarn's value; restrictions since early September.

phrases.Original example 2: They also allege that some exporters import yarn under bond facilities but sell it in the domestic market instead of using it to manufacture garments for export.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: imports under bond; yarn under bond; goods under bond facilities
phrases.Article headline: Yarn import row: PM asks committee to propose solution by 20 Nov
phrases.Exam value: Customs and RMG-trade phrase for Bank exams.

phrases.English explanation: The sequence of processes and firms involved in producing and delivering a product.
phrases.Original example 1: Comprehending it requires tracing the physical supply chain, decoding the nature of money flows, and examining the geopolitical tug-of-war between the rival superpowers.
phrases.Original example 2: The global supply chain divides into an interdependent hierarchy of specialists.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: physical supply chain; global supply chain; supply-chain disruption
phrases.Article headline: Demystifying AI finance: The supply chain, capital flows, and global rivalry
phrases.Exam value: Core modern-economics term for BCS/Bank English.

phrases.English explanation: A court punishment of death for a serious crime.
phrases.Original example 1: A Bangladeshi war-crimes court sentenced her to death last November in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising.
phrases.Original example 2: Hasina faces a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly 2024 crackdown.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: hand down a death sentence; face a death sentence; death sentence in absentia
phrases.Article headline: Hasina asks for new passport only to be denied by Bangladesh govt
phrases.Exam value: Standard legal collocation for BCS/Bank English.

phrases.English explanation: Behaving in a political way mainly to impress people rather than to achieve anything.
phrases.Original example 1: Chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said Hasina's recent activities, as reported by various media outlets, were merely political posturing.
phrases.Original example 2: For now, our comment is that she will not return and that these activities are political posturing.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: merely political posturing; political posturing by the opposition; empty posturing
phrases.Article headline: 'Merely political posturing': Bangladesh says Hasina has no intention of returning from India
phrases.Exam value: Political-commentary phrase for BCS current-affairs English.

phrases.English explanation: Orders received but not yet fulfilled; a pile-up of unfilled orders.
phrases.Original example 1: New business, business activity and employment continued to expand, while the order backlogs index also returned to expansion.
phrases.Original example 2: However, new orders, new export orders and factory output remained in contraction, while the order backlogs index continued to show sharp contraction.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: order backlogs index; growing order backlog; clear the order backlog

mcqs.question: The word 'bottleneck' most nearly means:

options.A: A narrow point that slows down a whole process or system
options.C: A container used for storing liquids
options.D: A wide road that speeds up traffic

mcqs.explanation: A bottleneck is a narrow point that slows down a whole process — here, chip foundries slow the AI supply chain.

mcqs.question: In the AI-finance column, TSMC is called a 'chokepoint' because it:

options.A: Controls the advanced chip manufacturing on which almost every tech company depends
options.B: Sells memory chips to phone makers
options.C: Designs chips for Nvidia and AMD
options.D: Writes the software that runs AI models

mcqs.explanation: TSMC owns the most advanced fabs; if its manufacturing paused, the global AI revolution would halt.

mcqs.question: The word 'staggering' most nearly means:

options.D: So large or surprising that it is hard to believe

mcqs.explanation: Staggering figures are so large they are hard to believe — here, hundreds of billions of dollars pledged for AI.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct synonym of 'interdependent':
mcqs.explanation: Interdependent means depending on each other — the AI supply chain is an interdependent hierarchy of specialists.

mcqs.question: The word 'gatekeeper' most nearly means:

options.A: A person or company that controls access to something important
options.B: A customer who buys goods at a gate price
options.C: A worker who guards a building at night
options.D: A lawyer who defends companies in court

mcqs.explanation: Gatekeepers control access — a handful of chip firms became gatekeepers of technological futures.

mcqs.question: ICB is 'facing a dilemma' over the Beximco Sukuk because:

options.A: It cannot recover the full amount by maturity, yet cannot declare a default while yields are still being paid
options.B: It has sold the Teesta Solar project
options.C: The Sukuk was fully repaid in 2021
options.D: It has already declared Beximco in default

mcqs.explanation: ICB lacks legal grounds to declare default because yield payments continue from Teesta Solar cash flows, but full recovery by 23 December is uncertain.

mcqs.question: The word 'expeditiously' most nearly means:
mcqs.explanation: Expeditiously means quickly and efficiently — Hasina's letter asked her request be processed expeditiously.

mcqs.question: A 'counterpart' is:

options.A: A person who disagrees with you in public
options.B: A bank account held in a foreign currency
options.C: A person holding a similar position in another organisation or country
options.D: A junior employee in the same office

mcqs.explanation: A counterpart holds a similar position elsewhere — Russia thanked its Bangladeshi counterparts after the IGC meeting.

mcqs.question: A 'plenary session' is a session:

options.A: Attended by all members of a body
options.B: Attended by only the senior members

mcqs.explanation: Plenary means attended by all members — the IGC protocol was signed after the commission's plenary session.

mcqs.question: The word 'recovery' in the PMI report most nearly means:

options.B: A government rescue package for banks
options.C: A fall in prices after inflation
options.D: A return to a normal or better state after a decline

mcqs.explanation: Recovery is a return to a better state — the economy recovered with a rebound in manufacturing, construction and services.

mcqs.question: What is a 'minimum wage'?

options.A: The average wage across all industries
options.B: The lowest wage an employer is legally allowed to pay workers
options.C: The highest salary a company may pay its workers
options.D: A bonus paid for overtime work

mcqs.explanation: A minimum wage is the legal wage floor — the workers' side proposed Tk 32,000 for Grade 4 RMG workers at the Minimum Wage Board.

mcqs.question: What is a 'green sukuk'?

options.A: A loan given to farmers for green agriculture
options.B: A share listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange
options.C: A Shariah-compliant bond funding environmentally friendly projects
options.D: A government bond sold only to foreign investors

mcqs.explanation: A green sukuk is a Shariah-compliant bond for green projects — Beximco's Tk3,000 crore Green Sukuk was the country's first private-sector one.

mcqs.question: According to columnist Sajed ul Islam, which company is the 'critical chokepoint' of the AI industry?
mcqs.explanation: The column argues TSMC, which owns the most advanced fabs in Taiwan, is the critical chokepoint of AI manufacturing.

mcqs.question: What did Sheikh Hasina ask Bangladesh for on 9 November 2026?

options.A: Release of jailed Awami League leaders
options.C: A new passport and national identity card to return from exile in India
options.D: A seat in the next parliament

mcqs.explanation: Hasina requested a new passport and NID so she could return from exile in India in December and surrender to a court.

mcqs.question: The Russia-Bangladesh protocol signed in November 2026 came from which meeting?

options.B: The 5th meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation
options.C: The 3rd meeting of the Joint Economic Council

mcqs.explanation: The protocol was from the 5th meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission (IGC) on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh Bank raised the overseas medical treatment remittance limit without prior approval from $15,000 to:
mcqs.explanation: The limit was doubled from $15,000 to $30,000 in the 9 November circular.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh validated its Multisectoral Action Plan for Eye Health for which years?
mcqs.explanation: The Multisectoral Action Plan for Eye Health covers 2027-2029 and was validated at a Dhaka workshop on 8 November.

mcqs.question: Where is the COP31 World Leaders' Summit being held on 11-12 November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: COP31's World Leaders' Summit is in Antalya, Turkiye, on 11-12 November; PM Tarique Rahman delivers Bangladesh's statement on 12 November.

mcqs.question: What was Bangladesh's overall PMI in October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: The overall PMI rose 3.2 points to 51.8 in October; 50.9 was manufacturing and 61.2 was agriculture.

mcqs.question: How many industrial groups joined the billion-dollar club in 2025-26?
mcqs.explanation: Nine groups crossed the one-billion-dollar threshold in 2025-26, up from eight in 2024-25.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh Bank's minimum-cash-margin directive for Ramadan imports remains in force until:
mcqs.explanation: The directive remains in force until 15 March 2027 under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act.

mcqs.question: When do this year's HSC supplementary examinations begin?
mcqs.explanation: The supplementary examinations begin on 1 December 2026 — which is why their passers cannot sit DU admission tests, whose applications close on 25 November.

mcqs.question: What minimum monthly wage did the workers' side propose for RMG Grade 4 workers?
mcqs.explanation: The workers' side proposed Tk32,000 a month for Grade 4 workers (Tk30,000 for apprentices); Tk45,000-60,000 is what a family of four needs to live decently.

mcqs.question: By when must Beximco repay the outstanding Tk2,800 crore of its Green Sukuk?
mcqs.explanation: The remaining Tk2,800 crore is due to sukuk holders by 23 December 2026.

mcqs.question: By when did the Prime Minister direct the committee to propose a solution to the yarn-import row?
mcqs.explanation: The committee led by the commerce minister must submit its recommendations by 20 November 2026.
